title: The branch a pull request targets is a setting, not wherever you are standing
description:
`baseOf` in packages/cli/src/board.ts:69 is `given ?? currentBranch(paths.root)`, so the branch a run is cut from and the branch its draft targets are both an accident of what happens to be checked out. Start a run while standing on `main` and SOBER opens a pull request into `main` — the release nobody asked for.

Give the target a home in `.sober/config.jsonc` under `dispatch` — the zod schema and the commented jsonc template both live in packages/core/src/config.ts, beside `draftPr` and `accept`. `baseOf` falls back to that setting before it falls back to the current branch, and the existing `--base` flag (packages/cli/src/index.ts:158) stays the per-invocation override. packages/core/src/pr.ts:125 already hands whatever it is given to `gh pr create --base`, so the publish path itself does not change. The same fallback has to reach the `accept`, `review`, `audit` and `reject` call sites in packages/cli/src/review.ts, which all go through `baseOf`.

Acceptance: a run started from any checked-out branch opens its draft against the configured target; `--base` still wins; a config with no target behaves exactly as today. Tests land with the code.

brief.approach: Complexity 5 / 10: the schema change is small, but the bootstrap lookup must preserve every CLI override and every review/accept call site while preventing accidental PRs into `main`. Add nullable `dispatch.base` beside the existing dispatch settings in `packages/core/src/config.ts`, defaulting to null for compatibility and documenting it in `DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT` as the branch new run branches and draft PRs target. In `packages/cli/src/board.ts`, keep explicit `--base` highest priority; otherwise use the checked-out branch only to bootstrap `readConfigFromBase`, return its configured `dispatch.base` when present, and fall back to the current branch when absent. A broken base-ref config must continue through the CLI’s existing refusal path rather than being silently ignored. Ensure `run`, queue draining, `review`, `audit`, `reject`, `accept`, and `accept --green` continue to call this single `baseOf` path; `packages/core/src/pr.ts` must remain a consumer of the resolved base and need no model of current checkout. Extend the nearest config and CLI/integration tests to prove a run started while checked out on `main` cuts from and opens its draft against configured `development`, `--base` still overrides it, review actions resolve against the configured target, and an omitted key behaves exactly as before. Update `.sober/config.jsonc` only if the generated/default configuration contract requires the repository’s checked-in example to carry `base: development`; do not create a changeset or release behavior.

acceptance.run: pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/config.test.ts test/integration/dispatch.test.ts test/integration/pr.test.ts
acceptance.proves: Config parsing, run branch creation, draft PR targets, review actions, explicit overrides, and missing-key compatibility are covered.

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'base' -- packages/core/src/config.ts packages/cli/src/board.ts && git grep -q -- '--base' packages/cli/src/index.ts
acceptance.proves: The target has a documented config home while the per-invocation override remains available.
All run and review call sites compile through the single resolved-base contract.
